{{Short description|Space of holomorphic functions on the open unit disk in the complex plane}}
In the [[mathematics|mathematical]] field of [[complex analysis]], the '''Bloch space''', named after French mathematician [[André Bloch (mathematician)|André Bloch]] and denoted <math>\mathcal{B}</math> or ℬ, is the space of [[holomorphic function]]s ''f'' defined on the [[open set|open]] [[unit disc]] '''D''' in the complex plane, such that the function 

: <math>(1-|z|^2)|f^\prime(z)|</math> 

is bounded.<ref>{{eom|last=Wiegerinck|first=J.|id=Bloch_function|title=Bloch function}}</ref> <math>\mathcal{B}</math> is a type of [[Banach space]], with the norm defined by

: <math> \|f\|_\mathcal{B} = |f(0)| + \sup_{z \in \mathbf{D}} (1-|z|^2) |f'(z)|. </math>

This is referred to as the '''Bloch norm''' and the elements of the Bloch space are called '''Bloch functions'''.
